identity.name: CREDITACCESS GRAMEEN LTD
identity.industry: Financial Services — NBFC-MFI transitioning to diversified rural retail lender

summary.oneLiner: The cleanest possible exit from the MFI credit cycle: PAT up 720% YoY to INR 493 cr, ROA 5.9% and ROE 24.4% on normalised asset quality (GNPA 2.18%, PAR 90 1.46%, X-bucket collection efficiency 99.68%), with AUM +16.4% YoY and retail finance now 20.6% of the book. The interesting tension is that management is *deliberately capping the run-rate* — retaining full-year guidance and planning 50 bps price cuts in Q3 and again in Q4 to hand the excess back to customers rather than print a 6%+ ROA, because cross-cycle ROA of 4.5% and ROE of 18-20% is the stated objective. The one-quarter-more wait is about El Niño and West Asia, not about the book.

> **Adjustments / one-offs:** the 720% PAT growth is a *base* artefact — Q1 FY26 was the trough of the MFI credit cycle. The honest run-rate signal is TTM ROA 4.0% / ROE 16%, which management itself put forward as the contextualising number. An **INR 41 cr overlay for the West Asia crisis** is already in the books. Stage-1 PCR is 1.63% (vs 1% a year ago) — described as the highest in the industry and effectively an embedded overlay. Q1 write-offs relate to stress that emerged in Q2 of the prior year; management states write-offs normalise from Q2 FY27.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 guidance retained in full, deliberately un-upgraded** — "we remain with the guidance today as it is so that we watch one more quarter before we take any further step." Reason given: El Niño and the second-order effects of the West Asia conflict, with the explicit caveat that "there's absolutely nothing on the ground" and "no leading indicators indicate any buildup of additional stress."
- **Pricing: ~50 bps rate cut around end-Q2/Q3 FY27, and potentially another 50 bps in Q4** — "maybe we may have to take 50 bps pricing cut in third quarter, maybe another 50 bps in fourth quarter. So it will happen gradually." Explicitly conditional on credit-cost behaviour; if credit cost stays elevated, no cut. Asset repricing takes 15-18 months to flow through.
- **Credit cost guidance 3-4% for FY27 maintained**, with the stated bias to "end towards the lower end" if no upside risk emerges. Q1 annualised was 2.8-2.9%.
- **Cross-cycle targets: ROA ~4.5%, ROE 18-20%.** Management explicitly refuses to *cap* current-year ROA — "we'll not be capping our ROA" — and conceded that if Q1 repeats, "we should be relatively doing much, much better" than the 4-5% band.
- **NIM: may fall to 13-13.5% if credit cost settles near 3%**, still delivering ~4.5% ROA. NIM and credit cost are explicitly managed as a pair.
- **Borrowing cost: started the year at 9.2%, may end ~9.4% average, "we may still hold around 9.3%"** — a 10-15 bps drift from the ECB/NCD tenor mix shift.
- **Medium-term: INR 50,000 cr AUM by calendar year 2028** (not financial year — clarified explicitly). **No capital raise required** — fundable from internal accruals.
- **Borrower additions: ~1 lakh per month average going forward** — the primary driver of MFI growth for the rest of the year (Q1 ran at ~83k/month).
- **Mortgage book needs ~INR 1,000 cr to reach full breakeven** including HO cost allocation.
- **Retail sourcing mix: 60% internal / 40% open market** steady-state for mortgages (currently 55/45); all other retail products 100% internal.
- **Stage-1 PCR expected range-bound at ~1.63%** next quarter unless the ECL committee raises weightings on West Asia/weather variables.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (lender). Funding pipeline is the analogue: **INR 9,440 cr of funding pipeline plus INR 2,993 cr undrawn lines** against INR 3,536 cr of cash. A **INR 425 cr private NCD issuance** was completed in the quarter to diversify the liability base. The stated FY27 liability priority is more ECB and NCD paper — longer tenor, better ALM, slightly higher price.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Group lending (MFI, ~79%):** AUM share of unique borrowers 45.7%; borrowers with >3 lenders down to 2.6% — evidence the deleveraging and MFIN guardrails are holding. 42 new branches added, total 2,276 across 457 districts; employees 21,981 (+3% YoY); **attrition down to 20.6% from 25.8%**.
- **Retail Finance (20.6% of AUM, up 250 bps QoQ from 18.1%):** 91% of it is the graduated unsecured business-loan (Unnati) book, already "significantly profitable like the group loans." Unnati customers average **7.7 years vintage and 732 credit score**; mortgage customers 6.2 years and 714.
- **Profitability by product:** all products profitable including mortgage (excluding HO allocation) except 2-wheeler, which is a small book. Business-loan-against-property yields ~20.5% (~1% below MFI) but with much lower opex and credit cost; ex-housing (~1% of AUM), 99% of the book yields 20%+.
- **Sourcing:** entirely by own employees — no DSAs or connectors. 2-wheeler uses dealer networks only for fulfilment, never sourcing; customers are handpicked from the internal base. Open-market mortgages carry a minimum ticket of INR 5 lakh; sub-INR 5 lakh mortgages are internal-customers-only.
- **Grameen Mahi app:** 4 lakh customers onboarded in Q1 alone, 15.4 lakh active = 34.5% of borrowers. Digital collections rose to **24.2% of total collections from 16.3% last year**.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Life-cycle finance / Project Shakti** is the strategic frame: graduate credit-tested, long-vintage MFI customers into higher-ticket secured retail products. The evidence offered is that a meaningful share of borrower households already carry retail credit alongside their MFI relationship, and that this diversification rises with vintage.
- **Grameen Mahi as an origination and collection layer** — management expects it to become an anchor for instant eligibility checks, small-ticket loan availment, lead generation for both new customers and retail products, and a unified cashless collection ecosystem. Framed as "a structural shift in how our customers choose to engage with us."
- Mortgage as the only product with meaningful open-market sourcing — the lever that could break the internal-graduation ceiling.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Balance-sheet compounding through the cycle:** net worth from INR 2,734 cr (FY20) to INR 8,347 cr (Q1 FY27) at 20% CAGR through four stress years (two COVID, two MFI credit cycle), of which **86% came from internal accruals** — "very few NBFCs in the country have delivered this pace."
- **Retail book held up through the last cycle:** PAR 30 in the Unnati book "never crossed around 3%… even at the peak of the credit cycle."
- **Highest Stage-1 provisioning in the industry (1.63%)** plus early classification (Stage 2 at 15 days, Stage 3 at 60 days) — absorbs risk earlier than peers.
- **People model as a genuine differentiator:** hire-fresh-and-promote-internally, protected incentive floors during stress periods, monthly *and* annual incentive structure. ~2,500 ex-employees expressed interest in rejoining during the last two years; ~700 taken back. Attrition 20.6%, "probably one of the lowest."
- **BRE (business rules engine)** allows credit policy to be tuned at product, customer and geography level and revised quarterly — the stated mechanism for making this up-cycle structurally better than the last.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 14.4% is described as *reflective of the last twelve months' credit cost*, not a permanent level — the framework is that NIM and credit cost move together to deliver the target ROA. If TTM credit cost drops from 4.0-4.5% toward 3%, NIM should fall to 13-13.5% via customer price cuts and still yield ~4.5% ROA. Cost-to-income is 29.3%; operating cost is described as "largely stable." Borrowing cost is essentially flat at 9.2-9.4%. Yield rose ~60 bps QoQ from a combination of lower interest reversals and a higher earning-book share; management expects it to "settle at this level for some time."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): 42 branches added in Q1 to 2,276 (+7.7% YoY). Branch and headcount expansion is described as **already budgeted in the plan** — no incremental spend is required to sustain the growth, which is why the excess profitability is being routed to pricing rather than to network investment. Mortgage needs to reach ~INR 1,000 cr of book to fully break even after HO allocation.
capital allocation: CRAR 24.9%; the INR 50,000 cr AUM ambition by CY2028 is explicitly **fundable without external capital**. Excess earnings have three stated uses and management has picked one: (1) pass to customers via pricing — chosen, from Q3; (2) additional overlay provisions — INR 41 cr already taken for West Asia, more possible if weather deteriorates, but constrained by a formal ECL committee process requiring backup data under Ind AS; (3) branch/people investment — already budgeted, so no incremental need. This is a rare case of a lender proactively giving back rather than compounding a windfall.
risks & watch-items:
- **El Niño / monsoon effect on rural cash flows** — no visible impact yet; management will watch 2-3 months before drawing conclusions. This is the stated reason for not upgrading guidance.
- **West Asia crisis** — no discernible business impact to date; INR 41 cr overlay booked; potential fuel-shortage escalation could force a higher Stage-1 weighting.
- **The ROE optics problem** an analyst pressed hard: a 24.4% Q1 ROE against a retained full-year guide implies either a large H2 slowdown or a bigger price cut than the 50+50 bps indicated. Management's answer — that the trailing-12-month recoup is deliberate and the cut is credit-cost-linked — is coherent but leaves the full-year print genuinely uncertain.
- **Mortgage book seasoning:** currently stable but on a very small base (~INR 270 cr per bucket); credit cost will become range-bound-but-rising as it scales.
- **KYC integrity** remains an industry issue (Aadhaar not permitted for MFI; voter ID is the common instrument); mitigation is multi-ID combinations plus e-KYC, but management could not quantify the exposure.
- Employee attrition, though improved, remains an industry-level structural issue that CA Grameen manages better than peers rather than one that is solved.
management quality / tone: High quality. The CEO volunteered the trailing-12-month ROA/ROE framing precisely to stop investors extrapolating the 720% PAT growth — "I want to spend a moment contextualizing our numbers appropriately." The CFO gave an unusually explicit walk-through of how NIM, credit cost and pricing interlock, including the concession that "otherwise, we will keep making 6% plus ROA. That is something which we would not want to obviously achieve on a continuous basis." Two direct questions were answered against interest: that they will not cap ROA (contradicting the conservative framing), and that a repeat of Q1 means "we should be relatively doing much, much better" than guidance. Refusals were narrow and reasonable (no specific customer flows). The one soft spot: the "we'll watch one more quarter" posture is being used to defer a guidance upgrade that the operating data already supports.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The retail-finance diversification is not ROE-dilutive**, contrary to the standard assumption. MFI share fell from ~100% to 79% with ROE intact because retail yields are within ~1% of MFI while opex and credit cost are "much, much lower." Ex-housing (1% of AUM), 99% of the book still yields 20%+.
- **Excess profit is being treated as a liability, not an asset.** The 50+50 bps price-cut plan means the market should model *lower* NIM in H2 as a sign of strength, not weakness.
- The Q1 write-off spike is a lagging echo of Q2 FY26 stress, not new deterioration — write-offs normalise from Q2 FY27, which will *reduce* reported credit cost mechanically.
- **Retail finance improves customer retention, not just yield:** "historically, we were losing our relatively higher vintage customers" — graduation is a defence against attrition of the best borrowers, and its 7-year average vintage is the compounding asset.
- The INR 50,000 cr AUM target is a **calendar-2028** number, not FY28 — a distinction management corrected on the call and one that models routinely get wrong.

hero.oneLiner: The cleanest possible exit from the MFI credit cycle: PAT up 720% YoY to INR 493 cr, ROA 5.9% and ROE 24.4% on normalised asset quality (GNPA 2.18%, PAR 90 1.46%, X-bucket collection efficiency 99.68%), with AUM +16.4% YoY and retail finance now 20.6% of the book. The interesting tension is that management is *deliberately capping the run-rate* — retaining full-year guidance and planning 50 bps price cuts in Q3 and again in Q4 to hand the excess back to customers rather than print a 6%+ ROA, because cross-cycle ROA of 4.5% and ROE of 18-20% is the stated objective. The one-quarter-more wait is about El Niño and West Asia, not about the book.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Framed as an inclusive-finance platform moving from "Providing access to affordable credit through microfinance" to "Partnering for growth through lifecycle finance", expanding the addressable market from one customer per household to the entire customer household via retail finance.
- Target segment stated as ~23.5 Crore low-middle income households by 2030, addressing a rural / semi-urban micro-retail credit segment the deck sizes at ~INR 70 Lakh Cr; primary customers are women, secondary customers are household members.
- Claimed accelerators are distribution and local mindshare: 16 states & 1 UT, 457 districts, 2,276 branches, >14,000 loan officers covering >4 lakh villages weekly, plus localised intelligence in informal segments and referral-driven organic leads.
- Cross-cycle credibility is the central argument — a decadal record spanning Demonetisation, Covid and the MFI credit cycle with 'Competitive Decadal Cross-cycle Performance: Growth: 29%, ROA: 3.4%, ROE: 13.9%' as stated by the deck.
- Strong parentage: CreditAccess India B.V. (Amsterdam) holds 66.21% of CA Grameen, is committed to holding up to the regulatory requirement, infused INR 550 Cr in FY17 post-Demonetisation and provides access to global fundraising.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Group lending (MFI, ~79%):** AUM share of unique borrowers 45.7%; borrowers with >3 lenders down to 2.6% — evidence the deleveraging and MFIN guardrails are holding. 42 new branches added, total 2,276 across 457 districts; employees 21,981 (+3% YoY); **attrition down to 20.6% from 25.8%**.
- **Retail Finance (20.6% of AUM, up 250 bps QoQ from 18.1%):** 91% of it is the graduated unsecured business-loan (Unnati) book, already "significantly profitable like the group loans." Unnati customers average **7.7 years vintage and 732 credit score**; mortgage customers 6.2 years and 714.
- **Profitability by product:** all products profitable including mortgage (excluding HO allocation) except 2-wheeler, which is a small book. Business-loan-against-property yields ~20.5% (~1% below MFI) but with much lower opex and credit cost; ex-housing (~1% of AUM), 99% of the book yields 20%+.
- **Sourcing:** entirely by own employees — no DSAs or connectors. 2-wheeler uses dealer networks only for fulfilment, never sourcing; customers are handpicked from the internal base. Open-market mortgages carry a minimum ticket of INR 5 lakh; sub-INR 5 lakh mortgages are internal-customers-only.
- **Grameen Mahi app:** 4 lakh customers onboarded in Q1 alone, 15.4 lakh active = 34.5% of borrowers. Digital collections rose to **24.2% of total collections from 16.3% last year**.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (lender). Funding pipeline is the analogue: **INR 9,440 cr of funding pipeline plus INR 2,993 cr undrawn lines** against INR 3,536 cr of cash. A **INR 425 cr private NCD issuance** was completed in the quarter to diversify the liability base. The stated FY27 liability priority is more ECB and NCD paper — longer tenor, better ALM, slightly higher price.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 guidance retained in full, deliberately un-upgraded** — "we remain with the guidance today as it is so that we watch one more quarter before we take any further step." Reason given: El Niño and the second-order effects of the West Asia conflict, with the explicit caveat that "there's absolutely nothing on the ground" and "no leading indicators indicate any buildup of additional stress."
- **Pricing: ~50 bps rate cut around end-Q2/Q3 FY27, and potentially another 50 bps in Q4** — "maybe we may have to take 50 bps pricing cut in third quarter, maybe another 50 bps in fourth quarter. So it will happen gradually." Explicitly conditional on credit-cost behaviour; if credit cost stays elevated, no cut. Asset repricing takes 15-18 months to flow through.
- **Credit cost guidance 3-4% for FY27 maintained**, with the stated bias to "end towards the lower end" if no upside risk emerges. Q1 annualised was 2.8-2.9%.
- **Cross-cycle targets: ROA ~4.5%, ROE 18-20%.** Management explicitly refuses to *cap* current-year ROA — "we'll not be capping our ROA" — and conceded that if Q1 repeats, "we should be relatively doing much, much better" than the 4-5% band.
- **NIM: may fall to 13-13.5% if credit cost settles near 3%**, still delivering ~4.5% ROA. NIM and credit cost are explicitly managed as a pair.
- **Borrowing cost: started the year at 9.2%, may end ~9.4% average, "we may still hold around 9.3%"** — a 10-15 bps drift from the ECB/NCD tenor mix shift.
- **Medium-term: INR 50,000 cr AUM by calendar year 2028** (not financial year — clarified explicitly). **No capital raise required** — fundable from internal accruals.
- **Borrower additions: ~1 lakh per month average going forward** — the primary driver of MFI growth for the rest of the year (Q1 ran at ~83k/month).
- **Mortgage book needs ~INR 1,000 cr to reach full breakeven** including HO cost allocation.
- **Retail sourcing mix: 60% internal / 40% open market** steady-state for mortgages (currently 55/45); all other retail products 100% internal.
- **Stage-1 PCR expected range-bound at ~1.63%** next quarter unless the ECL committee raises weightings on West Asia/weather variables.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Life-cycle finance / Project Shakti** is the strategic frame: graduate credit-tested, long-vintage MFI customers into higher-ticket secured retail products. The evidence offered is that a meaningful share of borrower households already carry retail credit alongside their MFI relationship, and that this diversification rises with vintage.
- **Grameen Mahi as an origination and collection layer** — management expects it to become an anchor for instant eligibility checks, small-ticket loan availment, lead generation for both new customers and retail products, and a unified cashless collection ecosystem. Framed as "a structural shift in how our customers choose to engage with us."
- Mortgage as the only product with meaningful open-market sourcing — the lever that could break the internal-graduation ceiling.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: NIM 14.4% is described as *reflective of the last twelve months' credit cost*, not a permanent level — the framework is that NIM and credit cost move together to deliver the target ROA. If TTM credit cost drops from 4.0-4.5% toward 3%, NIM should fall to 13-13.5% via customer price cuts and still yield ~4.5% ROA. Cost-to-income is 29.3%; operating cost is described as "largely stable." Borrowing cost is essentially flat at 9.2-9.4%. Yield rose ~60 bps QoQ from a combination of lower interest reversals and a higher earning-book share; management expects it to "settle at this level for some time."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: CRAR 24.9%; the INR 50,000 cr AUM ambition by CY2028 is explicitly **fundable without external capital**. Excess earnings have three stated uses and management has picked one: (1) pass to customers via pricing — chosen, from Q3; (2) additional overlay provisions — INR 41 cr already taken for West Asia, more possible if weather deteriorates, but constrained by a formal ECL committee process requiring backup data under Ind AS; (3) branch/people investment — already budgeted, so no incremental need. This is a rare case of a lender proactively giving back rather than compounding a windfall.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Balance-sheet compounding through the cycle:** net worth from INR 2,734 cr (FY20) to INR 8,347 cr (Q1 FY27) at 20% CAGR through four stress years (two COVID, two MFI credit cycle), of which **86% came from internal accruals** — "very few NBFCs in the country have delivered this pace."
- **Retail book held up through the last cycle:** PAR 30 in the Unnati book "never crossed around 3%… even at the peak of the credit cycle."
- **Highest Stage-1 provisioning in the industry (1.63%)** plus early classification (Stage 2 at 15 days, Stage 3 at 60 days) — absorbs risk earlier than peers.
- **People model as a genuine differentiator:** hire-fresh-and-promote-internally, protected incentive floors during stress periods, monthly *and* annual incentive structure. ~2,500 ex-employees expressed interest in rejoining during the last two years; ~700 taken back. Attrition 20.6%, "probably one of the lowest."
- **BRE (business rules engine)** allows credit policy to be tuned at product, customer and geography level and revised quarterly — the stated mechanism for making this up-cycle structurally better than the last.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **El Niño / monsoon effect on rural cash flows** — no visible impact yet; management will watch 2-3 months before drawing conclusions. This is the stated reason for not upgrading guidance.
- **West Asia crisis** — no discernible business impact to date; INR 41 cr overlay booked; potential fuel-shortage escalation could force a higher Stage-1 weighting.
- **The ROE optics problem** an analyst pressed hard: a 24.4% Q1 ROE against a retained full-year guide implies either a large H2 slowdown or a bigger price cut than the 50+50 bps indicated. Management's answer — that the trailing-12-month recoup is deliberate and the cut is credit-cost-linked — is coherent but leaves the full-year print genuinely uncertain.
- **Mortgage book seasoning:** currently stable but on a very small base (~INR 270 cr per bucket); credit cost will become range-bound-but-rising as it scales.
- **KYC integrity** remains an industry issue (Aadhaar not permitted for MFI; voter ID is the common instrument); mitigation is multi-ID combinations plus e-KYC, but management could not quantify the exposure.
- Employee attrition, though improved, remains an industry-level structural issue that CA Grameen manages better than peers rather than one that is solved.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [ECL model change] A revised ECL model was implemented, extending the historical period from 36 months to 120 months, adding three-scenario forward-looking modelling (stable period, major external events such as Demonetisation/Covid, and enhanced stress events) with separately computed PD and LGD and a regression-based macroeconomic model driving PD; total provisioning fell from 4.62% (Q1 FY26) under the earlier model to 3.20% (Q1 FY27) under the revised one.
- [Geopolitical overlay] Considering the on-going West-Asia crisis, the ECL model incorporates additional provisions of INR 41 Cr.
- [Restructured book] The Q1 FY27 total EAD of INR 30,121.7 Cr includes INR 200 Cr of restructured loans where provisioning stands at 40%.
- [Regulatory guardrails] Growth is described as being pursued 'in adherence with MFIN guardrails', with digital KYC and credit bureau checks plus MFIN guardrail adherence at onboarding, and the company positioning itself as sole lender to guardrail-adherent borrowers.
- [Funding action] A private NCD issuance of INR 425 Cr in the quarter is cited as further diversifying the liability base.
